name: Nedabiah
overview: Nedabiah is a male member of the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the son of Jehoiachin, also called Jeconiah. His mention is brief and specific, focusing on his lineage within the royal family of Judah. No additional notes provide further detail about his life or role.
namesAndTitles: The name Nedabiah means 'YHWH volunteers,' reflecting a theophoric element that honors God. This proper name is noted in 1 Chronicles 3:18 and does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful connection to divine willingness or service.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Nedabiah as the son of Jehoiachin, a king of Judah, establishing his place within the Davidic line. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Nedabiah's significance lies in his genealogical link to Jehoiachin, situating him within the royal lineage of Judah as recorded in 1 Chronicles 3:18. This connection underscores the continuity of God's covenant promises through David's descendants, which ultimately point forward to the Messiah. Although the biblical narrative does not elaborate on Nedabiah's personal deeds, his inclusion preserves the integrity of the Messianic line.
